content: 1. Fluconazole increases glipizide levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Fluconazole raises glyburide levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as strong CYP2C9 inhibitors may further decrease glyburide metabolism. 3. Goserelin increases fluconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Both granisetron and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Fluconazole increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose to half the recommended amount. No specific recommendations exist for immediate-release guanfacine. 6. Fluconazole and haloperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Histrelin increases fluconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Fluconazole increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Fluconazole and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Fluconazole increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Both hydroxyzine and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Fluconazole increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 13. Fluconazole increases ibuprofen levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 14. Fluconazole and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Fluconazole decreases ifosfamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing its therapeutic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Fluconazole increases iloperidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 17. Fluconazole increases imatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Fluconazole increases imipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Fluconazole and indacaterol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as QTc-prolonging drugs may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 20. Fluconazole and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 21. Fluconazole increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Fluconazole increases infigratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Fluconazole and inotuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and monitor electrolytes before and after initiation. 24. Fluconazole increases irinotecan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Fluconazole increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Fluconazole and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Fluconazole increases isradipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Fluconazole and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Fluconazole increases ivabradine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 30. Fluconazole increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the ivacaftor dose as per product-specific recommendations. 31. Fluconazole increases ivosidenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of QTc prolongation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Fluconazole increases ixabepilone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Fluconazole and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Fluconazole increases kola nut levels by reducing its metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 35. Fluconazole increases lacosamide levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 36. Fluconazole increases lansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 37. Fluconazole increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 38. Fluconazole increases lefamulin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Fluconazole increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 40. Fluconazole and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Fluconazole increases lesinurad levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 42. Leuprolide increases fluconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Fluconazole increases levamlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 44. Fluconazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 45. Fluconazole and levoketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Fluconazole and lithium both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Fluconazole and lofepramine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Fluconazole increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 49. Fluconazole increases lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 50. Fluconazole increases lopinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Each interaction specifies the mechanism (e.g., CYP enzyme inhibition), the clinical significance (e.g., QTc prolongation, increased toxicity), and the recommended action (e.g., avoid, adjust therapy, monitor closely).
